articles.body: Democrats won control of the Senate in the US midterm elections Tuesday, with initial results showing the party securing shock victories in Texas, Ohio, North and South Carolina, Kansas and Iowa.

articles.body: The polls in these midterm elections suggest that "this will either be a good night or a historic night for Democrats". But what is driving this momentum? We discuss this with our guest, Mallory Newall, Senior Vice President at Ipsos. "We've seen in our polling at Ipsos in recent weeks and months that voters have become increasingly frustrated with President Trump," she says.
articles.headline: US midterms: "Voters have become increasingly frustrated with President Trump"

articles.body: Tens of millions of Americans cast their vote in the crucial polls that have been pitched as a referendum on Donald Trump's presidency amid anger at surging petrol prices, tariffs and the Iran war. We discuss the first results with France 24's Kethevane Gorjestani and Fraser Jackson. "Even in places where the Democrats haven't won, the swing towards them has been significant", he says.
articles.headline: US: "Even in places where the Democrats haven't won, the swing towards them has been significant"

articles.body: Democrats notched a string of early victories in US midterm elections Tuesday, flipping a Republican-held Senate seat and making inroads in conservative House districts as President Donald Trump faced the prospect of a bruising election setback. France 24's Douglas Herbert gives us his analysis.
articles.headline: Democratic gains mount in US midterms as Trump faces bruising verdict

articles.body: Georgia Senator Jon Ossoff was reelected Tuesday to a second term, holding a key seat for Democrats by defeating Republican Representative Mike Collins in a race that catapulted the Senate’s youngest member to the forefront of his party’s national stars as it looks to stymie President Donald Trump in his final years in the White House.
articles.headline: REPLAY: Georgia Senator Jon Ossoff wins reelection

articles.body: With New Hampshire and Georgia staying in Democratic hands, Republicans now look to Michigan for a pickup, where Democrat Abdul El-Sayed is competing with Republican Mike Rogers. France 24's Jessica Le Masurier reports from a Democratic watch party in Detroit.
articles.headline: Midterms: Abdul El-Sayed, Mike Rogers face off for Michigan Senate seat

articles.body: Democrats have flipped a Senate seat in North Carolina as they try to recapture majorities in Congress and break Republicans’ unified hold on power in Washington. France 24's Florence Villeminot walks us through the US electoral map.
articles.headline: US midterm elections: Democrats flip Senate seat in North Carolina

articles.body: Roughly 6 in 10 voters deeply disapprove of US President Donald Trump's presidency, according to an AP survey released Tuesday. About 4 in 10 say the economy is the most important issue while 3 in 10 say the state of US democracy is of primary concern – well above the number that rated crime or immigration as most important.
articles.headline: US democracy, Trump fatigue, cost of living are top issues with voters, AP survey finds

articles.body: As Americans head to the polls for the midterm elections, François Picard welcomes historian Timothy Snyder, professor at the University of Toronto's Munk School of Global Affairs, for a conversation about the future of American democracy, the growing political influence of technology billionaires and the dangers of a new Gilded Age. Who really holds power in Donald Trump's America: the president or the billionaires surrounding him?
articles.headline: Historian Timothy Snyder: Trump running US foreign policy 'as though he were an organized criminal'

articles.body: As US voters cast their ballots in the midterm elections, the economy remained their top concern. Despite robust headline macroeconomic data, middle-class Americans are growing increasingly frustrated with the rising cost of living. Meanwhile, Donald Trump's tariffs have hit small businesses hard, leading to a significant rise in bankruptcies. Our correspondents met with some business owners.
articles.headline: Trump tariffs hitting small businesses

articles.body: In tonight's edition, Rwanda and South Africa will lose their duty-free access to the U.S. market after being excluded from the AGOA trade program. Also, South Africans head to the polls amid water shortages and frustration with local services. And in the DRC's mining capital, Kolwezi, residents are taking on one of the country's largest Chinese-owned mines... accusing it of poisoning their environment.
articles.headline: South Africa braces for some job losses as AGOA ends

articles.body: Donald Trump promised Americans a “Golden Age” when he returned to the White House in January 2025. Since then, his administration has slashed government spending through DOGE, ramped up mass deportations, expanded ICE operations and pursued an aggressive crackdown on DEI programmes and transgender rights. But how much has he actually achieved, and at what cost? Vedika Bahl examines Trump's domestic agenda since returning to office.
articles.headline: Trump promised a 'Golden Age'. What has he delivered at home?

articles.body: Will it be a trickle, a wave, or a tsunami? Election Day in the United States with Democrats hoping to take back one or both houses of Congress. We’ll track the turnout, gauge the mood and raise the curtain ahead of Midterms results that are sure to shape the last two years of Donald Trump’s second and final term. Will a US president who’s already broken norms with his maximum use of executive powers be affected by the results a little, a lot, or not at all?
articles.headline: Trickle or tsunami? Democrats eye gains in US midterm elections

articles.body: Around 200,000 cases of skin cancer are diagnosed in France every year. Yet as more and more patients seek medical advice, getting an appointment with a dermatologist is becoming increasingly difficult. Half the country's dermatologists are nearing retirement, and only around 100 new specialists are trained up each year. Faced with this growing shortage, some are coming up with innovative solutions. FRANCE 24's Aurore Dupuis and Sonia Baritello report.
articles.headline: France's dermatology crisis: Patients desperate for appointments

articles.body: Democrats are preparing to launch a flurry of investigations into President Donald Trump’s administration and business dealings if they retake one or both chambers of Congress, devising strategies to circumvent obstruction from the White House and avoid the impeachment deadlock that consumed the US legislature during Trump’s first term in office.
articles.headline: Family wealth, Epstein, ‘vanity projects’: How Democrats plan to investigate Trump after midterms

articles.body: As Moscow continues to launch strikes across Ukraine, Russian citizens are facing increasing financial strain. Since the start of the war in 2022, utility bills in Russia have risen by more than 50% – over 13% this year alone. These rising costs come as the country grapples with ongoing drone attacks originating from Ukraine.
articles.headline: Russian households face increasing financial strain as war in Ukraine drags on

These underground tactics, which Russian forces have been using for more than two years to slip past Ukrainian lines, are giving Kyiv a new strategy on the battlefield.
articles.headline: Ukraine and Russia are taking the war underground as drones saturate the battlefield

Polls have opened in dozens of US states in what is widely considered a referendum on Donald Trump. Most polls suggest Democrats will take back the House of Representatives, but could they also take the Senate and stymie Trump’s agenda during his final two years in office?

articles.body: In Texas, Democratic candidate James Talarico is leading the polls ahead of a high-stakes US Senate race against Republican Ken Paxton. The contest is one of the most closely watched battles of the midterm elections, with Democrats hoping to end a 30-year losing streak in the state. FRANCE 24's Andrés Espinal reports from Austin, Texas.
articles.headline: US midterms: Talarico seeks to break Democrats' 30-year losing streak in Texas

articles.body: AUSTIN — Democrats’ vision of a blue Texas is finally here. James Talarico has been elected a U.S. senator and Gina Hinojosa as governor, the first Democrats to win either office in more than a generation. The four other statewide candidates are leading as ballots continue to be counted. Democrats further down the ballot are leading some red districts, changing the complexion of the state legislature, congressional delegation and courts. “It’s something that I haven’t seen in decades, that none of us have seen in decades,” said former Texas House Speaker Joe Straus, a moderate Republican. It’s an outcome that even the most bullish Democrats didn’t dare enunciate in the late days of the election. But as results have poured in Tuesday night, the party is outpacing its expectations across the country’s second most populous state amidst a national romp. Both Hinojosa’s and Talarico’s victory margins came by running up vote counts in Texas’ deep-blue urban centers and while also leading in the largest Republican-led county in the country, Tarrant County. They reversed Republican gains across the Latino-heavy Rio Grande Valley region, an ancestrally Democratic area that had swung hard to the right in recent years. Democratic Rep. Vicente Gonzalez romped to a near-20 point victory in a seat Republicans drew to favor them during last year’s redrawing of the state’s House map, ousting a top Republican recruit who campaigned alongside Speaker Mike Johnson to begin election day. It amounts to a set of remarkable results in a state that hasn’t elected a Democrat to the U.S. Senate since 1988 and to the governor’s mansion since 1990. In recent cycles, Democrats have tried and failed to flip the state in presidential and U.S. Senate contests but have been largely uncompetitive for state offices. But Tuesday’s blue wave slammed into Texas particularly hard, as it combined frustrations over the economy, immigration enforcement, data centers and corruption with a collapse of Trump’s 2024 coalition. “We reminded voters that Republicans have been in charge in Texas for 30 years. That every problem we have, was caused by Republicans,” Michelle Lowe Solis, chair of the Bexar County Democratic Party. “They aren’t going to fix the problems, they caused them.” As votes continue to be counted, Democrats appear poised to blunt the impact of Republicans’ attempted gerrymander, likely sweeping the Rio Grande Valley congressional seats while holding onto another San Antonio-area district drawn to favor Republicans. In state Supreme Court races, they lead in all four seats up for grabs, potentially turning a 9-0 conservative majority into a 5-4 split. Among the first 36 state house races called by the Associated Press, 34 have gone to Democrats and just two to Republicans.“Voters aren't dumb,” said Rep. Linda Sanchez (D-Calif.), who chairs the Congressional Hispanic Caucus’ BOLD PAC. “Even though the Republicans have tried to cheat with the series of gerrymanders, that has, I think, only made voters in those areas more willing to participate.” Talarico’s and Hinojosa’s victories will be felt nationally. Texas Democrats, who have long asked for national money and resources in a state where elections are costly, now have a test case of how to win. And it will bolster their arguments that their state, with 40 electoral votes, should be treated as a presidential battleground. Ali Bianco and Jonathan Martin contributed reporting.
articles.headline: Democrats sweep Texas

articles.body: Just a few hours into election night, Republicans acknowledged what appeared to be a historic midterm defeat — a long-feared “blue wave” that had started washing across the nation. The extent of the washout became clear soon after polls closed: Republicans lost a South Carolina Senate seat for the first time in nearly 30 years. Democrats nipped on the heels of House incumbents in deep red Florida districts. And the man in charge of the party’s House reelection effort was at grave risk of losing his own seat. By 10 p.m., Democrats had already flipped three GOP House seats — itself enough to win a majority if Republicans can’t make gains elsewhere — and many in the party feared dozens more could follow as voters registered their dissatisfaction with President Donald Trump. Voters in Texas, a ruby-red state for a generation, appeared at risk of handing multiple statewide races to Democrats and possible control of the legislature. Joe Straus, a former state House speaker, cast it as a historic rebuke of an unpopular president. “President Trump hasn't exactly done any Republicans favors across the country,” he said on a POLITICO election night broadcast. “They haven't done themselves favors, frankly, by following so closely along.” Many of the political professionals charged with getting GOP candidates elected in this environment said the results could be potentially historic in nature. “We are looking at tsunami territory,” said one national Republican operative who, like others, was granted anonymity to candidly describe the returns. "This is the worst electoral defeat in my lifetime and likely in history," said another GOP operative working on battleground races. "Trump said his name and record was on the ballot and people responded — resoundingly." At an ill-fated victory party for Senate candidate Michael Whatley in North Carolina, staff were already packing up the room less than two hours after polls closed. Returns showed Democrat Roy Cooper on track to win by as many as 20 points in a race that was supposed to have been tooth-and-nail. Standing in the room, one North Carolina Republican openly pondered what many others in the party had long avoided saying openly — that it was finally time to think about life after Trump. “Trump has done some excellent things, and I appreciate that. But it can't be the party of Trump forever,” said Jonathan Fletcher, a former GOP county chair. “If the Republican Party is going to be serious about winning, we have to be serious about winning people in the middle.” Nearly every state, district and county shows movement toward Democrats, from counties that Trump won three times to blue strongholds where Democrats are improving their margins. County-level data shows Democrats doing on average more than 5 points better than Kamala Harris did in the 2024 presidential race. That suggests that districts Trump won by double digits just two years ago are in reach for Democrats. The losses threatened to pile up even after Republican candidates, committees and super PACs spent massive sums in an effort to retain control of Congress — including more than $380 million from President Donald Trump’s political operation. “I can’t believe how these House races aren’t close given the amount spent,” a senior Senate GOP operative said. Another senior Senate GOP official called it a “bloodbath.” Many of the Republicans said the war in Iran, which sent voters’ gas prices soaring, and continued frustration with the economy drove frustration with a party that won on those same issues in 2024. On top of that some quickly vented about substandard candidates — such as Darline Graham in the South Carolina Senate race and Ken Paxton in the Texas Senate contest. "Not only were folks upset about the war, inflation and gas prices, but add to that the fact they think he was making them eat a shit sandwich in Darline, and they just had enough," said Mick Mulvaney, a former Trump White House chief of staff and South Carolina congressman. Trump said on Truth Social his own absence from the ballot for the drastic Republican underperformance — even after barnstorming the country begging Republicans to “vote like I’m on the ballot.” “I wasn’t on the Ballot and if I was, we would have won IN A LANDSLIDE!” Trump posted shortly after 10:30 p.m. Other Republicans were ready to blame Trump’s own decisions. "Republicans got their asses kicked tonight because of the Iran war — plain and simple. Everything else is just noise and spin,” said a person close to the White House. Meanwhile, power in Washington was already shifting. The likely next chair of the House Oversight Committee, who has been gearing up for massive probes into the Trump administration, issued a two-word statement Tuesday addressed to administration officials and the “Trump Crime Family.” “Lawyer up,” Rep. Robert Garcia of California said. Will Steakin, Erin Doherty, Lauren Fedor, Ashley Ahn and Lisa Kashinsky contributed to this report.
articles.headline: The blue wave is cresting: GOP braces for midterm wipeout

articles.body: Joe Biden was unceremoniously ushered out of the White House two years ago. On Tuesday, he got a small measure of revenge. Prominent Biden administration alumni are winning in a handful of notable races, with Keisha Lance Bottoms — the one-time Atlanta mayor turned Biden’s senior adviser and director of the Office of Public Engagement — leading the pack by flipping Georgia’s governorship. The victories, his former staffers say, are an important part of rehabilitating his legacy within a Democratic Party that all but banished him in 2024. “It's proof that President Biden assembled a talented team of public servants — who the public is calling on now to help turn this country around,” said Ron Klain, Biden’s former chief of staff. “These fantastic men and women will make life more affordable, health care more available, protect our rights, fight corruption, and make our country stronger.” Biden was not a regular on the trail this year, and most Democrats kept their distance from the former president. But he did weigh in on a handful of primaries, helping put loyal lieutenants in front of voters who still held him in high regard. While Bottoms was the highest profile victory, there’s a number of Biden alumni also poised to head to Washington. Gabe Amo, who won a 2023 special election in a blue Rhode Island seat, secured his second full term in Congress. And Dan Koh, who won Massachusetts’ 6th District to succeed Rep. Seth Moulton, was Biden’s deputy Cabinet secretary and deputy director of the White House Office of Intergovernmental Affairs. He leaned into his Biden endorsement throughout the campaign and this week reposted a video of a phone call he and his family had with Joe and Jill Biden on primary night in September. “Mr. President and Madame first lady, thank you so much for all of your support,” he told them. “It wouldn’t have been possible without both of you. … You changed my life by giving me a job of a lifetime. And you got my back the minute I decided to run.” Biden’s Cabinet also had a strong night in other governor races. Xavier Becerra, Biden’s secretary of Health and Human Services, had a solid polling lead over Republican Steve Hilton in the race to be California’s next governor going into Tuesday. And, Deb Haaland, Biden’s Interior secretary, was projected to win the New Mexico governor race. "In his farewell speech, President Biden warned that ‘an oligarchy is taking shape in America of extreme wealth, power, and influence that literally threatens our entire democracy,’” said Andrew Bates, the former president’s longtime spokesperson. “He urged his team and supporters to keep standing up for the values that we all care about, including decency, hard work, and a sense of national community. On the ballot and off, a whole lot of his alumni are fighting to carry on that legacy.” CORRECTION: A previous version of this report misstated how many full terms Gabe Amo has served.
articles.headline: Biden’s revenge: His alumni are winning in the midterms

articles.body: Republicans don’t think their party is focused enough on their biggest issue. The economy — and specifically the cost of living — is far and away voters’ top concern, and new results from The POLITICO Poll reveal a warning sign for the GOP just hours before polls close: There’s a stark disconnect between what Republican midterm voters want their party to focus on and what they say the party actually is focusing on. Nearly half of Americans — 47% — say cost of living and affordability are among the issues that matter most when they are deciding how to vote. That includes a 44% plurality of Republican midterm voters and 54% of Democratic midterm voters. The economy and jobs ranked second. But when asked which issues matter most to their party, a 39% plurality of Republican voters cited immigration and deportations as a top priority for the GOP. Just 23% said the party’s top priority was cost of living and affordability — a 21-point gap from the share who said it was a top voting concern. Nearly two-thirds of Republican voters also say they want to hear more about the economy and cost of living from their party. It’s a clear signal that voters wanted the GOP to stay focused on affordability, even as some Republicans and President Donald Trump continued to lean into culture war attacks — from transgender athletes in women’s sports to calling Texas’ Democratic Senate nominee James Talarico “tofu Talarico.” In recent speeches, Trump has often prioritized other topics — including cultural issues, the Reflecting Pool and, yes, GOP candidates’ rear ends — over the economy. If Democrats win the midterms, “you will have a 1929 style economic depression,” Trump told a crowd in Daytona Beach, Florida this Friday. He added immediately after: “Because when you hear men in women's sports, when you hear transgender, when you hear about — you know, open borders and all — everything they have is crazy.” Meanwhile, there isn’t the same dissonance on Democrats’ side: A plurality of Democratic voters pointed to cost of living and affordability as a top priority for their party, the poll found. The findings expose a potential messaging vulnerability for Republicans heading into Election Day: Even among voters planning to support the party, there is a perception that GOP leaders are not devoting enough attention to the cost of living concerns weighing most heavily on Americans. Trump’s own agenda — his tariffs and his decision to involve the U.S. in a war with Iran — has roiled the country and key races that could determine balance of power in Congress. “Well, I don't think it's good for Republicans,” Republican strategist Jeff Burton said of the poll results. “But it makes sense, because most of the Republicans' campaign message hasn't evolved around that and what affordability and cost of living really is. And it's hard to tout it when every street corner has gas prices $2 or more than they were just a few months ago.” The survey, conducted by PF Global the weekend before the election, underscores the messaging challenge that has dogged Republican candidates throughout the cycle. Candidates in races up and down the ballot have zeroed in on economic talking points: Campaigns and outside groups have spent more than $800 million on ads focusing on affordability, including roughly $401 million from Democratic-aligned groups and $311 million from Republican-aligned groups, according to a POLITICO analysis of primarily TV ad data from the tracking firm AdImpact. Still, the GOP has struggled to effectively convince voters that it is doing enough to fix an issue voters also hold them responsible for. Some Republican strategists think that disconnect comes down to one person: Trump. “I mean, look at what he's doing today,” said longtime Arizona Republican strategist Chuck Coughlin on the eve of the election. ”He's going in front of the Lincoln Memorial reflecting pool. He's drawing attention back to his monument exhibition.” “It's phenomenal how off message he is, and how that has burdened the party with his narrative, which doesn't come close to talking about what Americans care about,” Coughlin continued. “I mean, he's pretty much said time and time again, he doesn't care. You know, he thinks affordability is a hoax.” At the end of last week, Trump made three campaign stops in Florida, South Carolina and Ohio. Across all of those speeches, he spent just over 10% of his time talking about the economy and the cost of living, according to a POLITICO analysis. That’s significantly less than the amount of time he spent talking about culture war issues and other topics unrelated to the affordability crisis. He spent more minutes advocating for Rep. Ilhan Omar (D-Minn.) to resign and zeroing in on the Dan Sullivan ballot controversy in Alaska than he did talking about prices and inflation, for example. Guns, transgender issues, and renaming landmarks took up more of his focus than taxes, tariffs, and drug prices combined. "President Trump has delivered on his promise to provide relief to hardworking families, securing more than $82 billion in individual tax relief from No Tax on Tips, No Tax on Overtime, the Enhanced Senior Deduction, and No Tax on Car Loan Interest,” White House spokesperson Matthew Middleton said in a statement. RNC spokesperson Natalie Baldassarre said “Democrats' far-left policies will decimate” Republicans’ progress and that Trump "has criss crossed the nation to drive voters to the polls to support our Republican candidates who will build on these achievements over the next two years." The POLITICO Poll suggests there is relatively little appetite among Republican midterm voters for more discussion of some of the cultural issues that have featured prominently in Trump’s political messaging. Just 10% of Republican midterm voters said they want to hear more about “wokeness and DEI” from the party, when asked to select two issues from a list of options. And only 6% of Republican midterm voters and 5% of Democratic midterm voters identified race, DEI and “wokeness” as among their top voting concerns. By contrast, 64% of Republican midterm voters said they want to hear more about the economy and cost of living and 42% said the same about immigration and border security. The results also underscore just how thoroughly the economy has dominated this election cycle, relegating issues that played prominent roles in past elections — including abortion rights and transgender issues — to the sidelines. “If Republican voters actually feel that their number one issue isn't being addressed, then that is definitely going to affect turnout,” said Burton, the GOP strategist. “And the worry could be that, ‘okay, they turn out, but do they actually vote Democrat or split their ticket?’”
articles.headline: Poll: GOP voters say the party isn’t focused enough on the economy

articles.body: Republicans’ 2024 coalition is cracking in real time. President Donald Trump roared back into office two years ago after making major gains with young voters and Americans of color. Now those key groups appear to be moving away from him amid an unpopular Iran war and his lagging approval ratings, according to new results from the POLITICO Poll conducted by PF Global. Roughly 9% of Trump 2024 voters plan to cast their ballot for a Democrat this year, compared with just over 2% of former Vice President Kamala Harris’ voters who now plan to back Republicans. Underlying that shift is a lack of enthusiasm from two groups central to Trump’s win: Latinos and young people. At the end of last year, 56% of Hispanic Trump voters identified as MAGA Republicans. As of this October, just 37% still do, revealing a frustration with the label that denotes some of the president’s most loyal supporters. At the end of last year, 50% of young Trump voters ages 20 to 29 said they were certain to vote. As of this October, just 38% say this. It’s an alarming sign for the party heading into election night, as Republicans race to save deep-red seats across the map and juice turnout among the MAGA base to avoid unthinkable losses. The scramble on the campaign trail reveals the extent of the concern. Speaker Mike Johnson is making one final campaign swing through South Texas on Tuesday, where Republicans have been racing to assuage Hispanic voters’ concerns over mass deportations and the economy. GOP officials are fretting about the impact of lingering inflation and high prices on working-class voters of all races, including young men they’re scared to death won’t show up to the polls in strong enough numbers. They’re also pouring millions of last-minute dollars into a series of southern states with large Black populations whose voters appear to be surging to the polls in record numbers — like Mississippi, South Carolina and even Louisiana — to shore them up. “The coalition that we built under Trump doesn't fucking exist anymore,” said Gina Swoboda, a longtime Trump ally and former chair of the Arizona Republican Party. The White House has been trying to stem the bleeding within the Trump coalition of voters: The president has barnstormed a series of largely red states and is holding a flurry of tele-rallies in the final days. “Two years ago, Trump and other Republicans had a play with those voters because they were frustrated with Biden and Harris; two years later, things might be less bad than they were two years ago — but they're still concerned,” said Scott Walker, the Republican former governor of Wisconsin and 2016 presidential candidate who now leads the conservative Young America's Foundation. White House spokesperson Lauren Bis said Trump has “crisscrossed the country” campaigning for Republicans and drawing a contrast with “the radical-left Democrats.” “President Trump is the unequivocal leader, best messenger, and unmatched motivator for the Republican Party,” Bis added. Natalie Baldassarre, a spokesperson for the Republican National Committee, said in a statement that the “Trump administration has delivered on its promises to the American people” and the president “has barnstormed the nation to tout these achievements.” GOP Latino voters start to shed the ‘MAGA’ label The durability of Republicans’ 2024 coalition is a crucial test for the party’s future. Republicans’ inroads with young, Latino and Black voters propelled the party into a trifecta of power in Washington, and keeping those gains will be key to the GOP’s bid to hold onto power. A regression in support from those groups could send Republicans back to the drawing board as they craft a winning formula for the 2028 presidential election. Top Republicans are incredibly worried about losing their grip on Hispanic voters, as they try to stave off a bloodbath in South Texas, losses across key Florida House seats and more. There’s been a 19-point drop between last November and this October of Hispanic Trump voters who identify as MAGA, part of Trump’s core base, according to the poll. While two-thirds of these voters still intend to vote for Republicans in the midterm election, their dissatisfaction with Trump’s agenda is clear. The survey found that Hispanic Trump voters are more likely than non-Hispanic Trump voters to have voted for Democrats in the past decade — and think the Trump administration’s mass deportations are too aggressive. Just one election season ago, Trump romped to victory in South Texas over Hispanic voters’ concerns about the border and the economy; Texas Republicans redrew the congressional map last year to make seats in South Texas even more favorable . But the Trump administration’s heavy-handed immigration enforcement, championed by senior White House official Stephen Miller, has sent Hispanics swinging back, according to four Hill Republicans, who were granted anonymity to discuss internal conversations. It’s harmed what once seemed like prime opportunities to unseat Democratic Reps. Vicente Gonzalez and Henry Cuellar, while endangering GOP Rep. Monica De La Cruz in a newly redrawn district the president won by 18 points in 2024. A group of Hispanic GOP lawmakers have continued to raise concerns directly to Johnson and senior White House officials. “Would I feel better if gas were $2.50 instead of $3.30? Yeah. But good luck convincing a guy things are getting better while ICE is picking up his uncle,” said one Texas Republican strategist, granted anonymity to speak candidly. The White House in response provided statements from Texas GOP Reps. Pat Fallon, Brandon Gill, Ronny Jackson and Lance Gooden defending Miller. “Hispanic Americans will continue to see that the Republican Party is fighting for the issues that matter most to their families, and Stephen Miller is absolutely leading the charge,” Jackson said. Senior Hill Republicans have been trying to salvage the imperiled South Texas House seats in a flurry of visits over the past few weeks. But they privately believe they reached the point days ago where no amount of money would stave off the impending disaster. “It’s the economy,” said Daniel Garza, the president of the Koch-backed LIBRE initiative and a Texas-based Republican strategist. Republicans’ vote share of Latino voters has increased steadily over the last decade, Garza noted, which is a long-term win for the party. But he says independent Latino voters have grown disillusioned since Trump’s return to office, especially on the economy. “I think they had higher expectations,” he added. Young Republicans aren’t certain they’ll vote One year ago, half of young Trump voters were certain they’d vote in this year’s election. But this past spring, that number dropped sharply: the percentage of young people who’d backed Trump who were certain they’d vote dropped by 11 points. As early as March , shortly after the war in Iran began, young GOP supporters began to voice their frustrations that the president had broken a core campaign promise. Other Republicans predicted that if the war lasted longer than a few weeks, its consequences would come back to bite the party at the ballot box. That chorus included influential voices like podcaster Joe Rogan, who has significant influence over young men. He had hosted both Trump and Vice President JD Vance on his show in the lead up to the 2024 election. Some Republicans are concerned that the big-tent team they formed just two years ago has been irreparably splintered — and their lack of a strong affordability message is to blame. “We forgot that we're a populist party,” said one Republican operative in Florida who was granted anonymity to candidly discuss the state of the GOP coalition. Areas like South Florida, and Miami-Dade County in particular, were central to Trump’s diverse, big-tent party: the president flipped the longtime Democratic county for the GOP for the first time since 1988 in 2024. “We went from being a very populist, scrappy kind of kumbaya party to this kind of almost elitist Republican Party,” they added. But even as Democrats see the prospect of significant wins and a crumbling GOP coalition, some warn they, too, haven’t found a winning message they can build on in future cycles. “It's like being in a relationship: You break up with someone and you have a little distance, and then you start romanticizing them,” said Michael Ceraso, a Democratic strategist and veteran of Bernie Sanders and Pete Buttigieg’s presidential campaigns. “I think [Democrats] all have recognized, very much in the summer, just to move out of the way. Because we're watching voters being like, ‘I want out of this relationship with Trump.’”
articles.headline: ‘We forgot what it's like to be populist’: Republicans see Trump’s 2024 crumbling

articles.body: Republicans have a trust problem on affordability, and Democrats are poised to inherit it. If Democrats do as well tonight as polls suggest, everyone knows the two reasons why: affordability and President Donald Trump. For a year now, The POLITICO Poll has consistently found that half of Americans rank the cost of living as one of their top three issues — and in a series of surveys this month, most Democratic voters say their vote is more about Trump than the candidates on the ballot. But our polling also reveals the challenges for a Democratically-controlled Congress. Democrats have opened up a strong advantage on affordability, but voters who are demanding action may quickly turn on a party that finds itself torn between competing priorities. Much of the Democratic coalition is approaching the midterms as a referendum on Trump, meaning a victory tonight would offer few clear lessons about what should come next. Democratic voters’ two biggest demands — drive down the cost of living and stop Trump — can also conflict, especially when it comes time to govern. Asked to choose between passing bipartisan legislation to reduce the cost of living or avoid giving the Trump administration any wins, Democrats are not united. Twenty-nine percent would prefer to sacrifice progress on affordability to help their 2028 chances. Here is what a year of The POLITICO Poll tells us about the electorate heading into the midterms — and what comes next. Other issues have risen and fallen, but the cost of living has remained in a tier of its own. Even as global instability rose in the spring, roughly half of Americans still ranked the cost of living among the country’s top three issues. The central test of the midterms has barely changed. Republicans’ problem isn’t just that voters are focused on cost of living – it’s that they increasingly trust Democrats to bring it down. Over the last year, Democrats have solidified support from their own base and made small gains among voters who went for Trump or sat out in 2024. That alone was enough to widen their advantage from 2 points to 17 points. Over half of voters supporting a Democratic candidate say their vote is more about Trump and his performance than the candidates themselves. That sentiment is particularly pronounced among progressives and those who have felt the squeeze of rising grocery and gas prices.This reveals a risk for Democrats. Learning how to beat Trump is less valuable than learning how to run candidates with popular platforms of their own — particularly with only two years left before he is no longer the president. Over the past year, we tested Democratic voters on a series of trade-offs between standing on principle and risking control of the House or the fight against Trump. They agreed on one thing: Lying to win is a bridge too far. Beyond that, Democratic voters are often split between principle and pragmatism. A narrow victory could sharpen the party’s progressive-moderate divide , but the larger question for a Democratic Congress would be how hard to fight Trump’s agenda. Before the 2024 presidential election, PF Global’s polling showed a dynamic that might sound familiar. Trump voters believed nearly every part of American life was getting worse. Now, under a Republican administration, their outlook has brightened — while Harris voters have grown markedly gloomier. The reversal shows how quickly partisan control shapes public perception. If Democrats retake Congress, they may gain not only the power to address voters’ problems, but the burden of solving them. Seb Wride is the head of polling at PF Global, the London-based firm that runs The POLITICO Poll.

"></img><p>Por mucho sentido dramático y mucho suspense que le pusiera <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-11-03/oscar-puente-dimite-por-dignidad-quiero-estar-a-la-altura-de-mi-pais.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-11-03/oscar-puente-dimite-por-dignidad-quiero-estar-a-la-altura-de-mi-pais.html">Óscar Puente a su dimisión</a>, el gesto no resuelve nada ni rebaja la vergüenza de una sesión parlamentaria que puso en escena el oportunismo y la indiferencia de los partidos ante los problemas de fondo. Nada invalida la reflexión que hizo Gabriel Rufián en su primera interpelación al todavía ministro, cuando dijo que la intriga de <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-11-03/puente-dice-que-comprende-que-le-pidan-la-dimision-pero-sigue-porque-no-ha-tomado-ninguna-decision-que-contribuya-al-accidente.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-11-03/puente-dice-que-comprende-que-le-pidan-la-dimision-pero-sigue-porque-no-ha-tomado-ninguna-decision-que-contribuya-al-accidente.html">su cese o su permanencia</a> era una distracción para perpetuar la confrontación política y evitar el único debate necesario: qué modelo ferroviario quiere España. La dimisión de Puente —tardía y con saturación de efectismo, pero no por ello menos justa e inevitable— puede satisfacer las políticas de la venganza y a quienes creen que la discusión se agota en el reparto de culpas, pero no soluciona nada. Ni siquiera parece que pueda propiciar una conversación sobre el sistema de transporte, que determina la cohesión, el carácter y la estructura misma del país. </p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/opinion/2026-11-04/el-debate-sobre-el-modelo-ferroviario-que-nunca-tendremos.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p>

articles.body: <p>Nadie lo sabía. Ni el mismísimo Pedro Sánchez. Óscar Puente ocultó al presidente del Gobierno su dimisión como ministro de Transportes hasta unos minutos antes de que la anunciara justo al final de su comparecencia en el Congreso para dar explicaciones por el accidente ferroviario de Urda. “Ha dado la cara, ha dado soluciones y, después, ha dado un paso al lado”, ha valorado Sánchez en un mensaje emotivo en redes sociales. El presidente ha destacado que la salida de Puente del Ejecutivo se produce “por dignidad” y “voluntad propia”. En definitiva, “por respeto a las víctimas y al proyecto progresista”. La conclusión de Sánchez es que el ejemplo de Puente “dignifica” a España “y demuestra que no todos somos iguales”. “Mientras unos solo dan lecciones, otros lo dan todo”, ha enfatizado en una andanada al PP. </p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/elecciones-generales/2026-11-03/sanchez-reivindica-la-dimision-de-puente-tras-dar-la-cara-demuestra-que-no-todos-somos-iguales.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p><img src="https://imagenes.elpais.com/resizer/v2/MIVQKWNEFREEFHMGBJQL2N56N4.jpg?auth=2c1db478a320764bd681d364cc4789fc8627b214ed47022f9caf55231cf534df" width="8192" height="5464" alt="Óscar Puente recibe el abrazo de Patxi López, portavoz del PSOE en el Congreso, este martes tras anunciar su dimisión."></img>

Durante su interrogatorio en la Audiencia Nacional por el<i> caso Leire Díez</i> y ante la insistencia del ministerio público para que respondiera quién le había pagado y si había una vinculación con el PSOE, <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-07-14/la-abogada-de-koldo-garcia-niega-que-el-psoe-pagara-su-defensa.html" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-07-14/la-abogada-de-koldo-garcia-niega-que-el-psoe-pagara-su-defensa.html">la letrada negó que el partido socialista</a> estuviese detrás, antes de acogerse al secreto profesional y avisar a la acusación de que no iba bien encaminada. “No tengo absolutamente nada que ver con el PSOE, y no ha pagado la defensa de Koldo respecto de mí”, repitió De la Hoz, que meses más tarde ha revelado (tras requerirlo ahora el juez instructor Santiago Pedraz) que la web ultraderechista <i>Okdiario </i><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-10-29/la-editora-de-okdiario-pago-242000-euros-para-costear-honorarios-y-gastos-de-la-defensa-de-koldo-garcia.html" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-10-29/la-editora-de-okdiario-pago-242000-euros-para-costear-honorarios-y-gastos-de-la-defensa-de-koldo-garcia.html">le abonó 242.000 euros por ese trabajo de defensa de Koldo García</a>.</p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-11-04/audio-la-abogada-de-koldo-garcia-advirtio-a-la-fiscal-de-la-sorpresa-que-se-llevaria-al-saber-que-okdiario-pagaba-la-defensa-no-tengo-nada-que-ver-con-el-psoe.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p>
articles.headline: Audio | La abogada de Koldo García advirtió a la fiscal de la “sorpresa” que se llevaría al saber que ‘Okdiario’ pagaba la defensa: “No tengo nada que ver con el PSOE”

articles.body: <img src="https://imagenes.elpais.com/resizer/v2/SN2OPXPATVAYZIQAACXVICEJWI.jpg?auth=ce19664c1aca55f5275b5de87c41a2256a38bde423e28ca8f44936151a134243" width="4000" height="2668" alt="La actriz y productora Stella Schnabel, esposa de James Chambers, en la sede de EL PAÍS el pasado jueves."></img><p>Stella Schnabel (Nueva York, 43 años), actriz y productora, acudió la pasada semana a la cárcel de Aranjuez (Madrid) para visitar a su marido, James Chambers, <i>Fergie</i>, que permanece desde julio en prisión provisional a la espera de que la Audiencia Nacional decida si aprueba su extradición a Estados Unidos. El país norteamericano reclama <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-08-09/fergie-chambers-el-activista-millonario-detenido-en-ibiza-soy-un-defensor-de-los-derechos-humanos.html" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-08-09/fergie-chambers-el-activista-millonario-detenido-en-ibiza-soy-un-defensor-de-los-derechos-humanos.html">al millonario activista propalestino</a> por supuestos delitos de lavado de dinero, disturbios y conspiración para cometer disturbios. Schnabel, embarazada de su segundo hijo en común con Chambers, niega las acusaciones y denuncia que su pareja sufre una “persecución política”. “Existe una creciente represión y una ola de fascismo bajo el mandato de Trump”.</p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-11-04/la-actriz-stella-schnabel-esposa-del-activista-millonario-encarcelado-en-espana-la-persecucion-a-propalestinos-es-una-obsesion-de-trump.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p>

articles.body: <p>Carmen Marcos y Rafael Hernández, ambos de 55 años, se conocieron en el instituto Fortuny de Madrid. Son novios desde los 16, en una relación que empezó en el aula. Y de cuyo amor nacieron Inés y Carmen. Ellas tres tienen hoy los ojos henchidos de felicidad. Ya no hay lágrimas. Están sentadas en la sala de espera de la Unidad de Cuidados Intensivos (UCI) del Hospital Universitario de Toledo, uno de los centros sanitarios donde <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-11-01/que-causo-el-accidente-la-secuencia-paso-a-paso-de-una-cadena-de-fallos-que-el-sistema-no-detuvo.html?mrfhud=true" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-11-01/que-causo-el-accidente-la-secuencia-paso-a-paso-de-una-cadena-de-fallos-que-el-sistema-no-detuvo.html?mrfhud=true">los heridos del accidente de Urda fueron derivados</a>. El miércoles se enteraron de que el tren en el que iba su marido y padre había embestido otro convoy. Rafael era pasajero en el primer vagón del AVE —el número 8—, uno de los más afectados y que se llevó por delante al Iryo. Desde entonces hasta este domingo por la tarde, Rafael había estado sedado con heridas muy graves. Pese al complicadísimo pronóstico y la asfixiante espera que arrancó el miércoles, ellas siempre confiaron en que saldría adelante. </p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-11-03/rafael-uno-de-los-pasajeros-del-primer-vagon-del-ave-despierta-de-la-sedacion.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p>

articles.body: <p>El comisario de Transportes, Apóstolos Tzitzikostas, todavía se muestra cauto a la hora de hacer valoraciones sobre el accidente ferroviario de la semana pasada en Urda (Toledo) que ha provocado la muerte de 69 personas. “Es demasiado pronto para decir nada concluyente sobre el accidente”, ha señalado este martes. No obstante, sí que ha apuntado que “la seguridad no es negociable” y que, para alcanzarla, la mejor solución es <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-11-03/transportes-reducira-la-circulacion-en-la-via-madrid-sevilla-para-separar-mas-los-trenes-hasta-que-este-en-pie-el-nuevo-sistema-de-seguridad-ertms.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-11-03/transportes-reducira-la-circulacion-en-la-via-madrid-sevilla-para-separar-mas-los-trenes-hasta-que-este-en-pie-el-nuevo-sistema-de-seguridad-ertms.html">“acelerar la implantación del sistema ERTMS en toda Europa”</a>, ha subrayado, en referencia al sistema europeo de gestión de tráfico ferroviario, en un encuentro con distintos medios de comunicación europeos, entre ellos EL PAÍS. </p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/economia/2026-11-03/bruselas-apuesta-por-reforzar-la-seguridad-ferroviaria-con-el-despliegue-del-sistema-ertms-en-toda-europa.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p>

articles.body: <p>Primero es el accidente de Adamuz (Córdoba), que deja 46 muertos. Luego, el de Urda (Toledo), con un balance de al menos 69. Ese doble golpe en apenas nueve meses pone el foco sobre el estado del corredor de alta velocidad Madrid-Sevilla, que afronta una compleja renovación tecnológica para combatir la obsolescencia de su sistema de seguridad LZB mientras soporta cada vez más tráfico. El uso de la ruta Madrid-Sur, que engloba el escenario de las dos tragedias, aumentó un 28% entre 2019 y 2024, y la oferta de plazas se disparó un 53% en ese mismo periodo, según datos de la CNMC. La competencia entre Renfe, Iryo y Ouigo aportó más trenes y pasajeros a una vía en plena actualización. En 2020, el Banco Europeo de Inversiones describió la infraestructura indicando que llegaba “<a href="https://www.eib.org/en/projects/all/20200385" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer" title="https://www.eib.org/en/projects/all/20200385">al final de su vida</a> de diseño”. En 2023, la Comisión Europea la tildó de “<a href="https://ec.europa.eu/regional_policy/projects/projects-database/infrastructure-upgrades-on-the-madrid-seville-high-speed-railway_en" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer" title="https://ec.europa.eu/regional_policy/projects/projects-database/infrastructure-upgrades-on-the-madrid-seville-high-speed-railway_en">desfasada</a>”. El Gobierno, según los datos oficiales, respondió con un significativo aumento de la inversión reforzado por fondos europeos: más de 800 millones. Sin embargo, el cambio del sistema de seguridad LZB por el ERTMS, adjudicado en 2021 con un plazo de 52 meses, e insistentemente reclamado por los operadores, sigue sin culminarse cuando llega el fatídico 28 de octubre: el cable está ya en su sitio, pero aún hay que hacer pruebas hasta final de año. </p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-11-03/el-uso-de-la-linea-del-accidente-de-urda-se-disparo-un-28-en-cinco-anos-y-los-operadores-reclamaban-sustituir-el-lzb-es-muy-importante.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p>
articles.headline: El uso de la línea del accidente de Urda se disparó un 28% en cinco años y los operadores reclamaban cambiar el LZB: “Es muy importante”

articles.body: (ACN) Tres vagons d’un tren de mercaderies han descarrilat i han xocat amb una locomotora a Martorell. Fonts de Renfe han informat que l’incident no ha provocat ferits . Tot i això, el maquinista que es trobava a la locomotora afectada ha anat a l’hospital, seguint el protocol establert, però es troba bé, segons indica la companyia ferroviària. L’accident s’ha produït només uns dies després del tràgic xoc entre dos trens a Toledo amb desenes de víctimes mortals, i el mateix dia que el ministre de Transports, Óscar Puente , ha presentat la seva dimissió . També et pot interessar Puente dimiteix: “És una qüestió de dignitat política, coherència i empatia amb les víctimes” Andrea Cuerva Bonich 2 minuts de lectura Ha descarrilat en una via privada Adif ha explicat que l’accident s’ha produït en la derivació particular de l’empresa de mercaderies Cargill, una via privada connectada a la xarxa ferroviària. En aquest tram, el tren de mercaderies feia una maniobra quan els tres vagons han sortit de la via i han acabat impactant contra la locomotora. Renfe ha assenyalat que aquest incident no ha afectat el servei de Rodalies . articles.body: Els repetits ciberatacs contra els sistemes de refrigeració de diversos supermercats a Europa genera preocupació. El darrer atac ha estat el matí d’aquest dilluns a Portugal, però establiments de França, Bèlgica, Finlàndia o Irlanda, entre d’altres, també n’han estat víctimes. Es tracta d’un ciberatac que dispara la temperatura de les neveres i els congeladors dels supermercats, la qual cosa ha provocat que es malmetin grans quantitats de menjar fresc i congelat . En una entrevista al programa bàsics , de betevé, l’empresa ControlTemp de Santa Perpètua de Mogoda que es dedica a registrar i monitorar la temperatura de neveres ha assegurat que és una situació que podria donar-se a casa nostra . Així ho ha concretat el seu gerent, Josep Domingo Romero, qui ha afegit que les grans superfícies de supermercats tenen les seves neveres i congeladors connectats a la xarxa i fan un control de la temperatura en remot a través d’internet , un aspecte que no passa a comerços més petits. “ Carrefour, Esclat, Lidl … hi ha moltes marques. Són grans superfícies que tenen moltes delegacions i necessiten tenir totes les neveres controlades”, ha explicat l’especialista, qui assegura que són supermercats que tenen els mateixos sistemes de control de fred que els supermercats que han patit atacs a Europa. També et pot interessar L’Agència de Ciberseguretat registra més de 6.500 atacs de hackers el 2025, el doble que fa un any Maria Solans 2 minuts de lectura La solució: un doble sistema de control Romero explica que els sistemes que tenen aquests tipus de supermercats inclouen alarmes de funcionament . El problema ve quan, en un context de ciberatac, sembla que l’ordre ve donava per un tècnic de dins el sistema. “L’equip entén que aquesta ordre és normal i l’alarma no salta”, ha detallat. És per aquest motiu que l’especialista ha puntualitzat que alguns supermercats tenen un doble sistema de control , tot i que no és habitual. “Es tracta de fer un control del fred, però en paral·lel també poder tenir un sistema que no depengui de la central que monitori la temperatura i enviï les dades al núvol sense estar connectat a la xarxa de l’empresa. Això et permet tenir una comparació “, ha detallat l’especialista. També et pot interessar Els intents de ciberatac, en augment: “A l’octubre ja vam superar la xifra de tot el 2024” Sandra García Prat 1 minut de lectura Recupera l’entrevista completa amb Josep Domingo Romero al bàsics

articles.body: (ACN) El ministre de Transports, Óscar Puente , ha anunciat la seva dimissió “per dignitat política” arran de l’accident d’Urda . “Un ministre de Transports no pot continuar en el càrrec amb dos accidents d’aquesta gravetat en menys d’un any , per molt diferents que siguin i tingui o no responsabilitat directa en aquests accidents: és una qüestió de dignitat política, coherència i empatia amb les víctimes “, ha sentenciat en la seva última intervenció durant la compareixença davant la Diputació Permanent del Congrés. Aquesta decisió, ha dit, “és bona per al país i bona per a la democràcia”. El ministre ha afegit que no serà tampoc cap de llista del PSOE per Valladolid. “ No tots els polítics som iguals “, ha conclòs. També et pot interessar 68 morts i 58 ferits en un accident entre dos trens d’alta velocitat a Toledo Marta Casals Torres 4 minuts de lectura Una decisió presa el dia de l’accident d’Urda Puente s’ha reservat per a la seva última intervenció l’anunci de la dimissió. Una decisió, ha afirmat, que va adoptar “en els primers minuts” després de tenir coneixement de l’accident , mentre es dirigia al centre de control de 24 hores d’Adif. Segons Puente, ha volgut fer pública la dimissió al Congrés i “un cop s’ha fet la feina més urgent i inajornable : fer les primeres investigacions per entendre què ha passat, adoptar les primeres mesures per a les víctimes i millorar, en la mesura del possible, la seguretat del sistema ferroviari a curt termini”. També et pot interessar Puente titlla d”‘inexplicable” la decisió del centre de control de fer reprendre la marxa a l’AVE Marina Sancho 2 minuts de lectura Una compareixença de quatre hores al Congrés Ha tancat així una compareixença en què ha rebut reiterades peticions de dimissió tant per part del PP i Vox com de la majoria dels socis de la investidura, tret d’ERC i EH Bildu. En la seva rèplica, ha insistit que no té responsabilitat “per acció o omissió” en l’accident. També ha insistit que sempre “ha dit la veritat” i ha “donat la cara” sobre l’accident, i ha afegit que “no té la resposta” sobre els motius pels quals l’operador d’Adif va adoptar “una decisió equivocada “. En aquest marc, ha rebutjat les “ anàlisis injustes ” sobre l’accident i ha explicat perquè el seu ministeri, i no ell directament, va apuntar a un error humà . També ha volgut desacreditar les “mentides” sobre les condicions laborals dels operadors que, segons ha explicat, treballen sis dies i en descansen quatre. “Jo no entraré si les condicions són millorables o no”, ha dit, però “els treballadors d’Adif estan sotmesos a les 37 hores i tenen condicions concretes”. articles.body: Per aconseguir el millor panettone de tot l’estat , el clàssic, el de fruita confitada i panses, haurem de fer uns quants quilòmetres fins a la pastisseria Vallflorida Xocolaters , a Sant Esteve de Palautordera, i tastar la proposta dels germans Lluís i Gerard Costa. Barcelona tampoc no ha guanyat en la categoria de xocolata, premi que s’ha endut la pastisseria La Roja , un establiment de la localitat d’Almoradí (Alacant). Els guardons s’han lliurat durant la segona jornada del Gastronomic Forum Barcelona . El pastisser Francisco Antonio Villagordo, de La Roja, ha reconegut que estava molt emocionat pel premi: “Porto molts quilòmetres a l’esquena, hem vingut molts anys a participar-hi. Tinc la sort de tenir un equip que em dona suport, ara intentarem gaudir del premi”. En la categoria de tradicional el guardó se l’han endut els germans Lluís i Gerard Costa de la pastisseria Vallflorida, a Sant Esteve de Palautordera. En el seu cas no és la primera vegada que guanyen perquè el 2023 es van imposar en les dues categories. La d’aquest 3 de novembre ha estat l’11 edició del concurs Millor Panettone artesà clàssic, mentre que la categoria de xocolata es premia des de fa sis anys. Rècord de participació Miquel Ángel Zaguirre, president de la junta directiva del Gremi de Pastisseria de Barcelona , ha reconegut que el panettone és actualment “un dels productes imprescindibles de la nostra pastisseria. Ens l’hem fet nostre. Tenen molta acollida per part dels consumidors i aquest concurs n’augmenta l’excel·lència. El dolç tradicional italià fa anys que s’ha colat a les nostres taules i celebracions, tant és així que cada vegada més obradors n’elaboren tot i la complexitat del producte. Una mostra del bon estat del panettone és que aquesta edició ha fet història amb un rècord de participació . Un total de 101 pastissers d’arreu de l’estat han portat el seu dolç a concurs: 50 de clàssics i 51 de xocolata. L’any passat van ser una setantena de participants al concurs organitzat pel Gremi de Pastisseria de Barcelona amb el suport de l’ Escola de Pastisseria del Gremi . També et pot interessar El millor panettone del món es fa a Barcelona, a la fleca artesana Suca’l Carmen Cortés Vidal Josep Bassas 2 minuts de lectura Els guanyadors de l’edició anterior del 2025, Oriol Carrió de la pastisseria Oriol Carrió (Bailèn, 216) en la categoria clàssica, i Rafel i Adrià Aguilera, de Cal Jan (Torredembarra), en la categoria xocolata, han format part del jurat juntament amb professionals del sector com el xef Paco Roncero i els pastissers Claudio Gatti, Ton Cortés, Iban Yarza, Alba Llacera i Miquel Zaguirre, Oriol Balaguer, Ramon Morató, Aniello Di Caprio, Anna Cortés i Jordi Luque. Els pastissers han valorat principalment el sabor, però també l’aroma, l’estructura de la molla, l’aspecte del glassejat i la forma. També et pot interessar El millor panettone tradicional de tot l’estat es fa a Barcelona, a la pastisseria Oriol Carrió Marc Bermejo 2 minuts de lectura Els millors panettones barcelonins Barcelona fa anys que recull el reconeixement dels panettones que es couen a les pastisseries de la capital catalana. L’any 2024, es va reconèixer el dolç de la pastisseria Mervier Canal i de Madeleine by Ferrieres , el 2022 el premi va ser per a L’Atelier i Panes Creativos i el 2019 el guardó va anar a Cloudstreet , forn Suca’l actual. Si anem encara més enrere, el 2018 trobem el panettone de Takashi Ochiai Pastisseria i el 2017 el millor dolç el va elaborar Oriol Balaguer. Els panettones barcelonins no només competeixen amb els millors dolços de l’estat, també ho fan amb les millors pastisseries del món. De fet, el pastisser Tonatiuh Cortés, el mestre forner de la fleca artesana Suca’l, va erigir-se amb el guardó de millor panettone del món . En la final a Milà d’enguany, el cap de setmana del 7 al 8 de novembre, Barcelona tornarà a estar present amb el panettone tradicional de Toni Vera de Mervier Canal i amb el dolç de xocolata de Roberto Juan del Forn del Barri .

articles.body: (ACN) L’escriptora i periodista Cristina Fernández Cubas ha estat distingida amb el Premi Cervantes 2026 , segons ha anunciat el ministre de Cultura, Ernest Urtasun. Llicenciada en Dret i Periodisme a Barcelona i casada amb l’escriptor Carlos Trías Sagner, és autora de contes i novel·les que li han valgut guardons com el Premi Ciutat de Barcelona el 2009 i el Premi Nacional de Narrativa de les Lletres Espanyoles el 2023. Urtasun ha estat l’encarregat de llegir la decisió del jurat, que ha destacat “l’originalitat, excel·lència i coherència d’una obra que ha renovat el conte contemporani i ha transformat la literatura fantàstica en espanyol” i que la situa com una de les figures “més importants” de les lletres hispàniques. El jurat també ha destacat la trajectòria “sòlida” de la guardonada, que ha contribuït “decisivament” a revalorar el relat breu “reivindicant-lo com una forma d’expressió autònoma capaç d’assolir la màxima intensitat estètica i profunditat existencials”. També et pot interessar Eva Baltasar guanya el prestigiós premi Médicis Étranger Clara Vera Colina 1 minut de lectura Ha publicat una vintena d’obres Nascuda a Arenys de Mar el 1945 i resident a Barcelona, Fernández Cubas va publicar el primer volum de contes, La meva germana Elba , el 1980. Des d’aleshores ha publicat una vintena d’obres. “A través d’una precisió narrativa impecable, el domini absolut del punt de vista i l’administració dels silencis —ha llegit Urtasun—, les seves històries es converteixen en experiències perdurables que interpel·len directament el lector i desestabilitzen les seves certeses en descobrir l’inquietant en el quotidià i qüestionar els límits de la realitat, la identitat i el coneixement”. També et pot interessar Enrique Vila-Matas, Premi Nacional de les Lletres Espanyoles 2026 Esther Castarnado 1 minut de lectura

articles.body: La previsió del temps per a aquest dimecres, 4 de novembre, anuncia una clara millora del temps , amb més clarianes, fred o fresca matinal, però una recuperació evident de la temperatura màxima. Previsió horària per a Barcelona: 6 h: núvols baixos i boirines 9 h: temperatures per sota dels 10 ºC 12 h: augment de les clarianes 15 h: ambient agradable, amb valors de fins a 18 ºC 18 h: alguns núvols baixos 21 h: nit fresca, amb mínimes de tardor avançada També et pot interessar Alguns indrets de Catalunya han quintuplicat aquest octubre la pluja habitual Marcos Amores Sánchez 2 minuts de lectura Les clarianes portaran un migdia molt més suau Després d’un dimarts rúfol i fresc, en què en alguns casos la temperatura van quedar fins a 5 ºC per sota la mitjana, el retorn del cel assolellat portarà un canvi de temps aquest dimecres. La màxima de l'Observatori Fabra avui, 3 de novembre, s'ha situat fins a 5 ºC per sota del que tocaria. L'absència clara de sol i l'entrada d'aire fred en altura n'han estat les responsables https://t.co/iHy5n6FpW3 pic.twitter.com/6X3RjyJf2y — btv el temps (@btveltemps) November 3, 2026 De bon matí, els núvols baixos i les boirines , fruit de l’ambient humit, podran ser protagonistes, especialment als punts més elevats de la ciutat. La màniga llarga ens serà necessària a primers hores, amb mínimes d’entre 8 i 12 ºC. A mesura que avanci la jornada, el sol anirà guanyant terreny , sempre amb el permís d’alguns núvols, i l’ambient anirà guanyant suavitat. Tant és així que la màxima es recuperarà de manera clara, amb uns termòmetres que, en molts casos, quedaran entre els 15 i 18 ºC. També et pot interessar Només un miracle impedirà que el 2026 entri al podi dels més càlids registrats a l’Observatori Fabra Marcos Amores Sánchez 3 minuts de lectura Nits de tardor però amb sol i suavitat pels migdies Pels propers dies no s’esperen gaires canvis a la vista, amb unes màximes més altes , però sempre dins d’un context de tardor. De cara a dijous , sembla que podrien tornar a guanyar terreny els núvols i algunes precipitacions per les comarques del sud. Per a divendres i el cap de setmana, el sol i els migdies de més de 15 a 18 ºC seran ben presents. articles.body: L’acampada pel dret a l’habitatge de la plaça de Catalunya s’ha mobilitzat aquest dimarts a la tarda per condemnar el desallotjament de l’acampada de Madrid . Malgrat la pluja, una trentena de persones s’ha concentrat davant del monument de Francesc Macià a la mateixa plaça per mostrar la solidaritat amb les persones desallotjades a la protesta madrilenya. En aquest sentit, els acampats asseguren que la idea és resistir a la plaça de Catalunya fins després de les eleccions generals del 29 de novembre per defensar el dret a un habitatge digne per a tothom. També et pot interessar Collboni no desallotjarà l’acampada d’habitatge, però avisa: la GUB està preparada per actuar si cal Roger Torres i Liñán 1 minut de lectura Un desallotjament de matinada El desallotjament de l’acampada de Madrid , a la Puerta del Sol, s’ha produït aquesta matinada. En total s’han desallotjat 334 persones i s’han detingut dues persones per desobediència i resistència. Per tot això, els acampats a Barcelona han mostrat la seva preocupació que aquesta actuació comenci una cadena de desallotjaments de campaments arreu de l’estat, incloent el d’aquí. De moment, des de l’acampada indiquen que no han rebut cap notificació de ningú per marxar . articles.body: La Guerra Civil va deixar més d’una cicatriu sota terra al carrer del 26 de Gener del 1641 , a Hostafrancs. Ja en el segon capítol de Jaciment Barcelona , els arqueòlegs hi van trobar no una, sinó dues entrades a refugis antiaeris. I van comprovar també que almenys una de les escales anava més enllà de la tàpia amb què el franquisme els va clausurar. Aquest quart episodi entra per primer cop des de fa 90 anys en aquestes galeries oblidades i ho fa amb la Unitat de Subsol dels Mossos d’Esquadra . Les imatges gravades durant la inspecció dels túnels són inèdites fins ara. Mossos de la Unitat de Subsol comproven l’estat semiesfondrat dels túnels del refugi També et pot interessar ‘Jaciment Barcelona’: Rambla, refugis i la feina del Servei i de l’Arxiu arqueològics [capítol 2] Francis Manzano Rojas 1 minut de lectura La vida aturada dins dels refugis No són els únics refugis protagonistes del capítol, que també segueix la pista de dos que es van trobar el 2023 al carrer de Piquer , al Poble-sec. En aquest cas, s’està fent ara la restauració dels objectes que s’hi van recuperar durant l’excavació i que inclouen des de llaunes de menjar a sabates, pintes i capses de pastilles Juanola . Algú va perdre o va deixar una sabata dins del refugi 410 del Poble-sec abans que es tanqués al final de la guerra I què se’n fa dels refugis després de l’excavació quan es troben al mig d’un carrer? La solució habitual és la que s’utilitza per cobrir un refugi incomplet que han trobat al carrer del Consell de Cent , tocant amb Independència. També et pot interessar ‘Jaciment Barcelona’: Correus, Fleming i Garcini [capítol 1] Francis Manzano Rojas 2 minuts de lectura El cim més estratègic per defensar la ciutat Barcelona, però, també es va defensar dels bombardejos d’una forma més activa. Ho va fer sobretot intentant foragitar l’aviació feixista des de bateries antiaèries com les del Turó de la Rovira , un espai recuperat fa uns anys gràcies a una intervenció arqueològica. Qui en va ser el director en descobreix tots els detalls. Les del Turó de la Rovira són unes de les bateries antiaèries més completes de l’estat Què hi feia un ase al costat de la muralla de la Rambla? A més, la sèrie torna a l’ excavació de la Rambla , que va començar en el segon capítol per continuar descobrint-ne el passat abans que fos un passeig. Una de les troballes que han fet al costat de la muralla medieval són unes restes excepcionalment completes d’un ase. L’ arqueozoologia , és a dir, l’estudi especialitzat d’aquest tipus de restes animals, en pot extreure informació molt valuosa per reconstruir-ne la història. També et pot interessar ‘Jaciment Barcelona’: el vaixell Ciutadella I, Correus i l’últim pont del rec Comtal [capítol 3] Francis Manzano Rojas 2 minuts de lectura Jaciment Barcelona consta de cinc capítols i és una producció pròpia de betevé en col·laboració amb el Servei d’Arqueologia de Barcelona . També et pot interessar ‘Jaciment Barcelona’: la docusèrie sobre recerca arqueològica que desenterra la història de la ciutat Francis Manzano Rojas 2 minuts de lectura

articles.body: (ACN) Els comitès d’empresa d’Adif i Renfe convocaran una vaga conjunta a les empreses ferroviàries públiques el dimarts 17 de novembre per reclamar millores de seguretat al sistema ferroviari. L’aturada es fa com a resposta al xoc de trens d’alta velocitat d’Urda el 28 d’octubre amb un balanç de 69 morts . Prèviament, els sindicats que formen part dels comitès han organitzat una concentració dels treballadors d’Adif i Renfe davant el Congrés dels Diputats el 16 de novembre , un dia abans de la vaga. També et pot interessar SEMAF convoca dos nous dies de vaga abans i després de l’11-N: el 10 i el 12 de novembre Marta Casals Torres 4 minuts de lectura Els sindicats demanen canvis En aquest context de mobilitzacions, la UGT traslladarà aquestes mateixes dates del 16 i 17 de novembre a la resta d’empreses del sector ferroviari per aconseguir una vaga sectorial. Per la seva banda, CCOO considera que la separació de Renfe i Adif va ser “un error” i reclama la constitució d’un grup públic d’empreses que recuperi la coordinació entre la infraestructura i l’operació ferroviària . També et pot interessar El Govern espanyol estudia aturar l’alta velocitat Madrid-Barcelona per fer-hi obres de millora Andrea Muñoz 3 minuts de lectura CCOO considera que la situació actual és el resultat del fracàs d’un model ferroviari imposat progressivament a través de les diferents directives europees, que ha afavorit la fragmentació del sistema. Per això, el sindicat també reclama la revisió dels protocols de seguretat a Adif i Renfe , plantilles suficients i formades adequadament i el reforç de la prevenció de riscos laborals i dels plans d’emergència. També et pot interessar Puente diu que no hi ha cap decisió presa sobre aturar l’alta velocitat Madrid-Barcelona Redaccio Societat Sandra García Prat 1 minut de lectura Alferro denuncia Óscar Puente En paral·lel, el sindicat Alferro ha denunciat el ministre de Transports, Óscar Puente , a la Fiscalia del Tribunal Suprem per les filtracions dels àudios del centre de control que es van publicar el mateix dia del sinistre als mitjans. En un missatge a la xarxa X, l’organització sindical ha exigit una “investigació rigorosa” i “sense anticipar conclusions” que assenyalin els treballadors. articles.body: El primer dia de l’Smart City Expo ha permès als milers de visitants que s’hi han apropat aquest dimarts, descobrir les principals innovacions urbanes, amb solucions pensades per fer les ciutats més sostenibles, eficients i segures. Si en les últimes edicions la cita prometia la implementació massiva de la intel·ligència artificial i la robòtica, en aquesta 15a edició ja és una realitat. A continuació detallem algunes de les novetats més destacades. També et pot interessar Comença l’Smart City Expo 2026, l’aparador de les solucions urbanes intel·ligents Cristina Brotons 4 minuts de lectura Terra 50 Una de les propostes rellevants és Terra 50: una iniciativa que reuneix 50 solucions urbanes de tot el món contra el canvi climàtic amb resultats comprovats i que es poden replicar en altres ciutats. El projecte es presenta a través d’ una experiència immersiva dins d’una cúpula , amb imatges enregistrades amb càmeres de 360 graus . Són imatges dels diferents paisatges de la Terra i serveixen per donar context a les diferents propostes que conformen Terra 50. Un codi QR convida l’espectador a llegir els detalls de cada projecte. La presentació del resultat ha estat enregistrada per l ‘artista immersiva Sofia Mellino, responsable del disseny visual. Entre els exemples hi ha la ciutat japonesa de Kamikatsu, que ha implantat un sistema de separació de residus en 14 categories i 44 subcategories per avançar cap a l’objectiu de residu zero. El bessó digital de Barcelona Si ens fixem en les iniciatives més properes, l’ Ajuntament de Barcelona presenta el bessó digital de la ciutat . Es tracta d’una eina que permet integrar dades de diferents àmbits per simular escenaris futurs i estudiar com es poden millorar els serveis i els espais urbans. Alex Gil, del Barcelona Supercomputing Center , explica que “el sistema permet incorporar tota la informació que tenim de la ciutat per poder veure quina és la realitat de cada lloc, redissenyar-la i planificar millores”. També et pot interessar betevé t’acosta la innovació urbana, en directe, des de l’Smart City Expo 2026 Actualitat betevé 3 minuts de lectura L’autobús 4.0 La innovació també arriba a elements quotidians com les marquesines dels autobusos . Les estructures incorporaran càmeres amb intel·ligència artificial capaces de detectar el volum de passatgers en cada moment. L’Eugeni Rico, cap del Centre de Serveis del Centre de Mobilitat i Espai Públic, explica que aquesta informació arribarà al centre de control de mobilitat, podrà prendre decisions per adaptar el servei a la demanda i millorarà la gestió del transport públic. Un bomber robòtic La robòtica és un altre dels àmbits que guanya protagonisme en aquesta edició. Un dels exemples és la seva contribució i ajuda al servei dels Bombers de Barcelona. Al saló es pot veure un robot programat per l’extinció del foc. Funciona com un cotxe teledirigit i té una àmplia capacitat de moviment i de desplaçament. Gerard Prades, cap de la Unitat de Bombers de Barcelona, assegura que els “permet protegir millor els efectius i accedir a zones de més risc per l’humà per reforçar la seguretat en les intervencions”.
